absent: Behavior of filename parent resolution and helper entry points for unlink, symlink, link, and rmdir.
Contracts of permission, security, delegation, and filesystem rename methods invoked by rename.
Semantics of dentry move and exchange, mount detachment, and dcache shrinking on victim replacement.
Mount reference counting, propagation busyness, namespace semaphore ownership, and full unmount teardown.
Page cache write transaction details and address space operation failure modes for symlink storage.
Full fsnotify, audit, and mount listing show formatting beyond the sampled inline calls.
Numeric values of user visible rename, lookup, and unmount flags and error mappings not stated in fragments.

findings.text: Removal exposes an extended entry with directory descriptor plus pathname plus flag word and a legacy entry with pathname only. The extended form rejects flag bits outside directory removal, routes directory removal separately from file removal, and the legacy form behaves as the extended form with a current directory reference.

Symbolic link creation and hard link creation each expose a directory relative form and a current directory form. Both resolve old and new pathnames independently, forward directory descriptors, and for hard links also forward caller option bits to a common helper. The plain forms default descriptors to current directory.

Renaming exposes a flag carrying entry plus two flagless compatibility entries. All resolve old and new pathnames then delegate to one shared rename helper, with compatibility entries supplying a zero option word and the plain rename defaulting both descriptors to current directory.

The shared rename helper accepts only three option bits for no replace, exchange, and whiteout. Exchange cannot be combined with either of the other two. Invalid combinations fail before any lookup side effects beyond pathname handling.

Rename requires both parents on one mount, requires normalized final components, and maps a non normalized target under no replace to an existence failure. Non directory sources reject trailing separators, and non exchange targets reject trailing separators when the source is not a directory, while exchange targets that are not directories also reject them.

Rename has two retry loops. Delegation conflicts repeat only the locked rename phase after waiting, and stale handles repeat the whole lookup with revalidation requested. Write hold is released before the outer retry and reacquired on the next attempt.

Core rename is a no operation when source and target are the same object. Otherwise it checks deletion rights on the source and creation or deletion rights on the target, with exchange checking deletion against the target type. Cross parent directory moves additionally require write rights on moved directories, followed by a security gate before locking.

Core rename locks victims and moved subdirectories under rules distinguishing directory and non directory cases. Cross parent moves lock the source subdirectory, exchange and victim handling lock the target as needed, and pure non directory pairs use an address ordered helper. Unlocking mirrors which side was actually locked.

After locking, rename vetoes swap files, mount points, and link count overflow on cross parent directory creation. It then breaks delegations on affected parents and non directories, invokes the filesystem method, updates dentry placement unless the filesystem claims that work, and emits move notifications only on success.

Symbolic link reading offers a cached fast path, a legacy method fallback, and a default path that promotes an inode to default handling under its spin protection. The default path reuses an already present link or obtains one with deferred cleanup, then copies a bounded prefix to user space.

Link retrieval for path walking only acts on symlink dentries. It first applies a readlink security check and only then calls the inode link method, returning invalid for non symlinks and propagating security or method failures.

Page backed links share one folio acquisition helper with distinct behavior for absent versus present dentry context, one requiring already valid cached content and the other permitting blocking fill. A raw variant returns the mapping address directly, a cooked variant ensures termination bounded by page size, and a release helper drops the folio reference.

Page backed symlink storage loops over a filesystem write transaction pair. It preserves non filesystem allocation context around the begin phase, copies payload less terminator, and repeats the transaction when the filesystem reports a short write, marking the inode dirty only on full completion.
Page backed symlinks publish an inode operations table whose link resolution service is the terminating page helper. No other methods are provided by this table in the fragment.

Move notification emits a combined rename record plus separate removed from and moved to records sharing one cookie, with directory variants of all masks when the moved object is a directory. It then updates target link count observation, self move observation, and child audit state.
In this configuration the notification cookie helper is a constant zero valued function of no inputs.
Link termination writes a zero byte at the lesser of supplied length and supplied maximum, guaranteeing termination within the caller buffer bound.
User readlink copying truncates link length to the caller buffer size and reports a fault value if the user store fails, otherwise reports the number of bytes stored.

Mount attribute change parameters group paired set and clear masks with propagation and lookup controls, plus a small kind flag word and references to a user namespace and an idmap. The kind flags distinguish recursive application from idmap replacement, assigned to the first two bit positions.
A mount cover record links into a parent cover table and separately into a pin table that keeps its mountpoint, and carries a dentry pointer plus a mountpoint pointer plus deferred reclamation state.
A pinned mountpoint record links into a pin list and carries a mountpoint reference together with its parent mount reference.
Mount unique identifiers start at two raised to the thirty first power, and a global counter is initialized to that base.

Mount table defaults include a one hundred thousand entry system control limit, boot time size parameters for mount and mountpoint hash tables, an initramfs options string hook, a global event counter, an emptied namespace pointer, filesystem object identity, and private null filesystem instances.

Mount namespace teardown releases the passive reference and only then drops user namespace and storage. An RCU callback adapts that release to deferred context, and lookup by identifier takes a passive reference under RCU on success.
Namespace identifier lookup runs under an RCU guard and relies on RCU delayed freeing of the final reference to safely acquire a new passive reference.

Mount reclamation is deferred through RCU callbacks and a batched workqueue drain. One callback frees a mount object, another performs full cleanup, and the worker detaches the whole pending list before cleaning each entry.

Mount lifetime marking distinguishes long term internal mounts from short term ones. Creation for long term use tags the result internal after success, making short term clears that association, and internal cloning duplicates from a path with private propagation then sets the internal mark.
Mountpoint testing first checks a dentry flag without locking, then under RCU repeats a mount sequence protected predicate until the sequence is stable.

Mount identifier search walks an ordered tree and returns the smallest identifier at or above the target in the forward form and the largest identifier at or below the target in the reverse form, with exact matches stopping early.

Mount listing iteration holds the namespace read lock across the sequence. Start seeks by position identifier, next follows the tree successor or moves position past the current identifier at end, stop releases the lock, and show delegates formatting of the current mount.

Unmount busyness checks hold the mount hash lock while walking the propagation tree and comparing reference counts with a higher allowance for the tree root. The single mount form additionally holds the namespace read lock around the whole check.
Internal unmount tree options use value one for synchronous behavior and value two for propagation and value four for cover handling.

Unmount exposes a two argument entry and a legacy one argument entry sharing one kernel helper. The helper rejects flag bits outside force, detach, expire, and nofollow, maps nofollow to mountpoint lookup without following, resolves the user pathname relative to current directory, then delegates to path based teardown.

Rename must not lock unrelated directories across parents without the global filesystem rename mutex, must reject swap files and mount points after locking, and must enforce link limits on cross parent directory insertion. Victim directories are marked dead and detached from mount visibility before dentry replacement.

Page link acquisition asserts absence of high memory mapping constraints, readlink copying silently truncates oversized links to user length, and unmount fails invalid flag words before path resolution.
